title: The gateway that double-billed every retry
blurb: Retries counted twice and close ids re-minted.
prompt: A customer's invoice showed twice their traffic, because the draft counted every gateway retry and then re-closed the billing period under a fresh close id. A crash also silently dropped the last minute of usage. Review it, fix it, and prove counts and closes are idempotent.
aiNote: The draft has no request-id dedupe, so gateway retries inflate usage, and its period close mints a new id per attempt, so a retry after a timeout can bill a period that already closed under a different id.
testIdea: Replay a usage report three times and assert one count; time out the billing flush and assert the period stays open and the retry reuses the close id; crash between response and count and assert the record and counter agree after recovery.
followUps: What sanity cap belongs on per-request units?
How do you reconcile metering with gateway logs?
